$about: THE SSR FIELD-WIRING ROUND. Branch experiment/base-ui, 11 August 2026.
Phase A left `gate:html` at 12 named-controls violations, down from 98, and
attributed all 12 to select.tsx with the note that the fix was STRUCTURAL and
needed form.tsx ported. This round names each of the 12 from real bytes,
finds the seam phase A said did not exist, and measures a SECOND half of the
same defect class that no gate rule can see: aria-describedby.
Nothing committed. `gate:html` was NOT re-run — it requires `next build`,
which this brief forbids on RAM grounds — so the residual count below is a
PROJECTION with its evidence stated, not a measurement. That distinction is

$finding: All twelve are ONE component in ONE shape: Base UI's `<button role="combobox">`
from `Select.Trigger`, preceded by a sibling `<label>` that carries neither
`for` nor `id`. Six Select instances, each prerendered in two locales.
NONE of them is a correct skip. `useSsrLabelId` was never reached by any of
them — select.tsx did not call it and could not, so this is not the hook
declining to relabel an already-named control. It is a second mechanism.
The number to fix was 12, not fewer.

instances.state: DISABLED — tabindex=-1, disabled, showing the raw key `thr` as its value

the_twelve_named_individually.source_confirms_the_shape: apps/website/src/examples/select.tsx — four demo variants, every one `<Select placeholder=…><Label>…</Label><SelectTrigger/>…`. No demo passes aria-label.

the_control_case.$why_it_matters: if aria-label were also broken at SSR the fix would be a different one.
the_control_case.evidence: view-block/en-US/preferences/index.html renders `<button … role="combobox" aria-label="Display language">` and is NOT a violation. Base UI passes an aria-label PROP straight through during render. Confirms the gap is the label-ASSOCIATION machinery, not the attribute.

was_it_a_second_mechanism.answer: yes, and phase A's diagnosis of the cause was right while its diagnosis of the fixability was wrong
was_it_a_second_mechanism.mechanism_1_already_fixed: checkbox / switch / number-field — the WRAPPER renders the label, so it can mint an id and thread it to both elements. That is what took 98 → 12.
was_it_a_second_mechanism.mechanism_2_the_twelve: select — the CONSUMER renders the label as a sibling. The wrapper never sees it, so there was nothing to thread.
was_it_a_second_mechanism.phase_a_said: 'there is no seam to inject through without either cloning children or making form.tsx's Label context-aware. The real fix is porting form.tsx's Label onto Base UI's Field.Label, which touches every field component in the library.'
what_is_actually_true: form.tsx's `Label` is ALREADY context-aware and always was. It is RAC's
`LabelContext` is a PUBLIC export of react-aria-components. Nothing in the
tree was providing it — that is the entire defect.
Verified by rendering rather than by reading: a `<Label>` under
`<LabelContext.Provider value={{id, htmlFor}}>` emits both attributes in
`renderToStaticMarkup`, and an explicit `id` on the element still wins over
the context one. `<Description>` behaves the same through `TextContext`'s
`description` slot, which is how the same trick would extend.
So the twelve cost one context provider in select.tsx and NO change to
form.tsx, and the library-wide port phase A sized is not required for them.
That port may still be wanted for other reasons; it is no longer a blocker.

why_nobody_had_measured_it.not_an_oversight: no gate rule can see it
why_nobody_had_measured_it.named-controls: grades accessible NAMES; a described-by-nothing control is fully named
why_nobody_had_measured_it.resolved-idrefs: deliberately excludes aria-describedby — its own docblock explains why (React Aria legitimately emits post-hydration describedby targets at SSR)
why_nobody_had_measured_it.consequence: violation count for this half was, and would remain, 0 while the help text under every Persian checkbox and switch went unannounced to a no-JS or pre-hydration reader. It is recorded here at full weight rather than being reported as 'clean'.

describedby_verdict.wcag: 1.3.1 / 4.1.2 — the description is programmatically present and programmatically unassociated

what_was_built.returns: paired props: labelProps, controlProps, descriptionProps, errorProps
what_was_built.ids: all minted from ONE useId() with stable suffixes, so a component pays one hook slot and server and client agree
skip_semantics_preserved: an explicit aria-label or aria-labelledby suppresses the whole naming arm — a <Checkbox aria-label="انتخاب همه"/> in a table header is never relabelled
an explicit aria-describedby suppresses the whole describing arm
an id is minted only for content the caller is ACTUALLY rendering, so a reference can never outlive its element

two_modes_and_why.aria: wrapper owns the label → control points at it with aria-labelledby. The only route that works for Checkbox and Switch at all, whose control is a <span role=…> and therefore not a labelable element.
two_modes_and_why.native: consumer owns the label → the LABEL points at the control with htmlFor and the control carries the id. Chosen for Select because the wrapper cannot prove a label exists, and an aria-labelledby minted on that guess would be a dangling idref — trading one defect class for another. htmlFor on an element that never renders emits nothing.
two_modes_and_why.both_routes_measured: a <button role="combobox"> named by label[for] and one named by aria-labelledby BOTH satisfy the shipped named-controls rule; the native arm is chosen on the dangle argument alone, not on the grader's opinion.

size.per_component_cost: one hook call plus up to four prop spreads
size.distribution_cost: select.tsx now travels with base-ui-adapter.ts. Confirmed against the real generator: build-registry.mjs picks the new companion up (select's item goes from 1 file to 2, registryDependencies unchanged at [popover]). registry.json was NOT left regenerated — the brief forbids committing and a sibling agent is editing this tree.

a_third_instance_found_while_wiring.what: <CheckboxGroup label=…> served <div role="group"> with neither aria-labelledby nor aria-describedby
a_third_instance_found_while_wiring.why_it_was_invisible: named-controls grades its INTERACTIVE selector, which does not include role=group. Zero violations, real loss.
a_third_instance_found_while_wiring.note: checkbox.tsx's own docblock says Base UI's CheckboxGroup 'emits role="group" aria-labelledby={labelId}'. It does — the id is simply undefined until a layout effect runs. The docblock was right about the code and wrong about the bytes.
a_third_instance_found_while_wiring.status: FIXED by the same hook, and pinned by the fixture

a_defect_found_and_NOT_fixed.what: `<FieldError>{errorMessage}</FieldError>` renders NOTHING. Measured: renderToStaticMarkup(<FieldError>خطا</FieldError>) is the empty string — RAC's FieldError needs a FieldErrorContext, and nothing provides one inside a Base UI NumberField.Root.
a_defect_found_and_NOT_fixed.consequence: a caller-supplied validation message on NumberField never reaches the page, in any tier. It is not a naming defect; it is a missing element.
a_defect_found_and_NOT_fixed.why_not_fixed_here: out of this brief's scope, and it is the same unported-form.tsx root cause one component further along. Recorded rather than silently worked around; the wiring hook is deliberately NOT given `errorMessage` in number-field.tsx, because an aria-describedby pointing at an element that does not render is the dangling idref this round exists to avoid.

what_this_round_did_not_cover: No browser rendered anything, and no build was run. Every claim is about renderToStaticMarkup output and the phase-A prerender on disk.

Hydration is checked at ONE point — that the checkbox's name and description still resolve to the same elements after effects — and not for Select, whose trigger id is now Lumo's rather than Base UI's. A real hydration-mismatch tier would be needed to make that claim properly.
The describedby fix has no gate rule behind it. It is held by one fixture in one package.
form.tsx is still unported. That is now a choice rather than a blocker for the twelve, and it remains the blocker for NumberField's dropped error message.

TextContext (the description-side twin of LabelContext) was verified to work but is not used: Select has no description in its public API, and wiring one would reintroduce the dangling-reference risk the native mode exists to avoid.

does_this_move_comparison_md.axis_1a_dangling_idrefs: unchanged — this fix adds none, and the Select arm was deliberately designed so it cannot
does_this_move_comparison_md.axis_1b_unnamed_controls: the residual goes 12 → 0 (projected). Base UI's disadvantage here is now fully workaroundable from OUTSIDE with public props, which is the thing this branch was built to test, and the answer is yes.
does_this_move_comparison_md.the_cost_that_does_not_go_away: every one of these workarounds compensates for an implementation choice — registration inside a layout effect — not a documented seam. Base UI can change it in a patch release and every one of these components goes quietly unnamed again. That is a smaller, cheaper tax than React Aria's 27KB node_modules patch, and it is still a tax, and it now covers describedby as well as labelledby.
does_this_move_comparison_md.the_new_line_item: the describedby half was never in any count on either engine, because no tier could see it. Both engines' numbers on this axis were measured with an instrument that does not detect it.
